El Niño 2026–27 · October to January · 17 countries

Where will El Niño hit food security this season, and what can decision-makers do now?

A very strong El Niño is under way. Its effects differ from place to place: floods in one country, failed harvests or salt in the rice fields in another. This tool uses GeoAI to turn scattered forecasts and reports into one map per country, showing where the hotspots are, which crops are exposed during the October–January season, and what to do about it.

The problem

El Niño is predictable months ahead, yet food crises it causes keep catching governments late. Forecasts say the Pacific is warming; they do not say which districts lose their harvest, which crops are in the ground, or when relief has to arrive. That translation is usually done by hand, country by country, too slowly.

Why it is hard

The evidence is scattered across climate centres, meteorological services, water agencies, FEWS NET, FAO and the press, in many languages and formats. El Niño also works in opposite directions: wetter in East Africa, drier in southern Africa, Southeast Asia and Central America. And the same rain matters differently at planting than at harvest.

What this tool does

For each country it groups provinces into impact zones, rates the El Niño tendency and crop stage for October–January, flags food security hotspots on a four-level scale, and lists interventions that can be taken before the impact peaks, each tied to a cited source.

How GeoAI produces each map

  1. 1Climate signalLive ENSO and ocean indices from NOAA CPC and IRI: strength, timing and duration of El Niño.
  2. 2Regional evidenceSeasonal outlooks, water and crop assessments, food security reports and FAO anticipatory-action guidance, retrieved and cited.
  3. 3Geospatial layersProvince and district boundaries grouped into impact zones, joined to crop calendars, reservoirs, rivers and salinity points.
  4. 4Governed AI synthesisThe SERVIR platform assembles an evidence pack; the AI drafts against it; a groundedness gate checks citations and issues a replayable receipt.
  5. 5DecisionsHotspot levels and interventions per zone, with a priority table for each country.

Hotspot levels used on every map
